q.en: Which is an example of a support/enabling activity in the P3O Value Matrix?

en: Ensuring programme outcomes are in line with business strategy
Checking whether the delivery of initiatives is on schedule
Managing the delivery of programmes
Providing tools to assist Project Managers in delivering projects

x.en: Providing tools to assist Project Managers in delivering projects Correct: Providing tools, templates and data to assist Project Managers in delivery is a support/enabling activity. Ref 2.4.2.2/Fig 2.2

q.en: Which statement regarding P3O assurance functions and services is FALSE?

en: Carries out audits of its own P3O functions
Provides independent assurance in addition to that provided by a Programme Board
Takes various forms including regular health checks
Provides guidance in the start-up stage of projects

x.en: Carries out audits of its own P3O functions Correct: The P3O itself should be subject to independent assurance and external audit and should not therefore audit its own functions. Ref 3.3.4

q.en: Which is a definition of business as usual?

en: The integration of the concept Run the Business, Change the Business' into the portfolio
The way the business normally achieves its objectives
Totality of an organization's investment in the changes required to achieve its strategic objectives
A coordinated collection of strategic processes that enable the most effective balance of change and business as usual

x.en: Ref 1.3.1, business as usual (BAU) is The way the business normally achieves its objectives.

q.en: Which of the following offices has the key role of asking 'Are the right things being done'?

en: Temporary Project Office
Centre of Excellence (COE)
Programme Office
Portfolio Office

x.en: Ref 1.5.1, Portfolio Office asks 'are the right things being done and in some organizations the key question to ask might be how can we stop so many of the wrong things'

q.en: Regarding to the process of developing a balanced portfolio, Which statement is considered FALSE?

en: When resources are limited, existing programmes / projects should have priority over new initiatives
It is necessary to take into account both operational and strategic priorities
Termination of existing change initiatives not aligned to an organization's strategic objectives may be necessary
Operational improvements may be stopped while projects offering greater strategic contribution are delivered

x.en: Ref 1.3.1, Existing programmes and projects that are not aligned to strategy may be realigned or terminated or put on hold while higher priority initiatives which support strategy are delivered.

q.en: What is defined as a temporary, flexible organization created to coordinate the implementation of a set of related projects and activities?

en: Project
Programme
Portfolio
Business as usual

x.en: Ref 1.3.2, Programme: A temporary, flexible organization structure created to coordinate, direct and oversee the implementation of a set of related projects and activities in order to deliver outcomes and benefits related to the organization’s strategic objectives. A programme is likely to have a life that spans several years.

q.en: Within a P3O, Which of the following does NOT describe services delivered by the appropriate office?

en: Portfolio Offices should facilitate the optimization of business change activities
Portfolio Offices should be compatible with business as usual governance structures
Project Offices should compare the consistency of different projects
Programme Offices should assist in delivering programmes consistently and well

x.en: Ref Tab 1.2, Portfolio Offices and COEs, not Project Offices, support consistent delivery of change across an organization. A COE may also provide independent assurance to ensure this consistency.

q.en: Which defines what a P3O provides?

en: Integration with governance arrangements and other corporate support functions
Decision-making entire organization.
Replacement for Programme and Project Boards
Decision-making forum for Programme and Project Managers

x.en: Ref 1.4, (P3O) The decision-enabling and support business model for all business change within an organization. This will include single or multiple physical or virtual structures, i.e. offices (permanent and/or temporary), providing a mix of central and localized functions and services, and integration with governance arrangements and the wider business such as other corporate support functions.

q.en: From the followings which is NOT related to project management?

en: Achieving outcomes
Planning a project
Motivating a team
Monitoring a project

x.en: Ref 1.3.2, Programme management is the coordinated organization of a dossier of projects and transformation activities to achieve outcomes.

q.en: Which of the following would a portfolio progress/change delivery committee is most useful?

en: Oversight information showing project and programme highlights
Project Closure Reports
Investment choices
Programme identification briefs

x.en: Ref 1.6, Where portfolio management is implemented, this usually means that decisions about inclusion in the portfolio will lie with the portfolio direction group/investment committee and responsibility for oversight of portfolio progress will lie with the portfolio progress group/change delivery committee. So, 'Oversight information showing project and programme highlights' is the correct option, but the others options are likely to be useful for portfolio direction groups rather than progress.

q.en: To assess return on investment/benefits, Which office triggers post-programme reviews to assess investment/benefits?

en: Portfolio
Programme
Virtual
COE

x.en: Ref 1.5.1/Fig 1.3, The Portfolio Office triggers post-programme reviews to assess return on investment/benefits.

q.en: What describes a hub connected by spokes model?

en: No physical, central office, P3O functions are carried out by business or functional units across the organization
An organization model with multiple, decentralized, permanent offices designed to serve specific divisions or functions
A single, permanent, organization-level portfolio office with temporary programme and project offices
A portfolio, programme and project management standards unit, which defines standards, skills and training

x.en: Ref Table 1.2, The Hub and Spoke office is a permanent office set up to support the definition and delivery of a portfolio of programmes and projects within a department, division, geographical region or business unit.

q.en: Rules relating to escalation of risks should be agreed in a P3O model with multiple offices. Why?

en: Allow every decision to be made at organizational board level
Enable multiple sources for a single piece of risk data
Allow every Programme Manager to display risk information in a different way
Enable a decision to be made by the right group based on the right information

x.en: Ref 1.6, Where a P3O comprises multiple offices, rules regarding escalation of risks should be established to ensure the right decision is taken by the right person or group based on the right supporting information.

q.en: Which of the following are governance responsibilities of a P3O model? 1.Ensure the right level of decision is taken by the right person or group based on the right level of supporting information 2.Provide approval at a stage gate without other sign-off if all issues are resolved 3.Equip management boards with exception reports and associated options 4.Provide appropriate rules for summarizing progress information?

x.en: Ref 1.6, ensuring stage gates are not passed through without the appropriate authority and sign-off, by giving management boards the correct information to decide on progress, e.g. progress reports, exception reports and options. not as mentioned in point#2 "Provide approval at a stage gate without other sign-off if all issues are resolved"

q.en: What should a P3O recommend when a 'must do' change does not directly contribute to an organization's strategic objectives?

en: No new change should be started until the 'must do' change has completed
Strategic objectives and priorities should be reviewed in the light of the 'must do' change
Must do' change should be stopped
Must do' change should be realigned to existing objectives

x.en: Ref 1.3.4, When a 'must do' change does not deliver any of the organization's strategic objectives, the objectives may need to be changed and priorities reviewed.

q.en: From the followings, Which are considered as objectives of a COE?

en: Provide training and skills transfer to the PPM community in defined standards
Support the delivery of a specific change initiative being delivered as a programme
Support the definition of a portfolio of change across an organization
Support the delivery of a portfolio of change in a geographical region

x.en: Ref Tab 1.2, A COE defines standards and provides skills and training.

q.en: Which of the following describe the relationship between change and business as usual? 1.Programmes deliver change into an organization's business operations environment 2.Business stakeholders must be engaged appropriately about the changes being delivered 3.Programme delivery should take priority over business as usual activities 4.Disruption to business as usual needs to be considered when planning changes?

x.en: Ref 1.3.4, Point #3 is not correct because of ' PPM and business as usual are integrated and collaboratively realize strategic objectives'.

q.en: Identify --------- and evaluate the true implications of the aggregate level of programme and project risk' What are the missing words in the statement which describe the decision support role of a Portfolio Office?

en: Concerns and suggestions
Issues and opportunities
Threats and opportunities
Roles and responsibilities

x.en: Ref 1.5.1, 'identify threats and opportunities and evaluate the true implications of the aggregate level of programme and project risk'

q.en: The relationship between business as usual and change can be described by which statement?

en: Business as usual should always take priority
Change initiatives should always take priority
Decisions affecting either must consider both elements of an organization
They are separate activities that can survive independently

x.en: Ref 1.3.4, Business as usual and change may be regarded as separate activities but cannot survive without each other. Therefore, any decisions relating to either need to be made collaboratively at the correct level.

q.en: What is a Programme Office?

en: Permanent office set up to support the delivery of a portfolio of change across the entire organization
Permanent office set up to develop standards to be applied to programmes and projects within a division
Temporary office set up to support delivery of a specific change initiative being delivered as a programme
Temporary office set up to support delivery of a specific change initiative being delivered as a project

x.en: Ref Table 1.2, Programme Office is a temporary office set up to support delivery of a specific change initiative being delivered as a programme

q.en: PPM is a common abbreviation, What does it stand for?

en: Project, Programme and Portfolio Matrix
Portfolio, Programme, Project Maturity
People, Process and Product Management (including Value and Risk Management)
Portfolio, Programme and Project Management (including Value and Risk Management)

x.en: Ref 1.2, PPM stands for Portfolio, Programme and Project Management including Value and Risk Management (PPM).

q.en: Which of the following offices can a P3O model consist of? 1- permanent only 2- Temporary only 3- Both permanent and temporary 4- Neither permanent nor temporary?

x.en: Definition: Portfolio, Programme and Project Offices (P3O) The decision-enabling and support business model for all business change within an organization. This will include single or multiple physical or virtual structures, i.e. offices (permanent and/or temporary), providing a mix of central and localized functions and services, and integration with governance arrangements and the wider business such as other corporate support functions. Ref erence Introduction Page 7.

q.en: Which is a permanent office supporting the definition of a portfolio of programmes and projects within a geographical region?

en: Project Office
Hub Portfolio Office
Organization Portfolio Office
Programme Office

x.en: Hub portfolio office: A permanent office set up to support the definition and delivery of a portfolio of programmes and projects within a department, division, geographical region or business unit.

q.en: Which describes an objective of portfolio management?

en: Coordinate the implementation of a set of related projects and activities
Enable the most effective balance of organizational change and business as usual
Achieve outcomes and realize benefits that are of strategic importance to the business
Collect in one place all of the information about an organization's investment initiatives.

x.en: Definition: portfolio management A coordinated collection of strategic processes and decisions that together enable the most effective balance of organizational change and business as usual. Ref Introduction Page 5

q.en: How does a P3O model increase an organization's ability to deliver its strategy?

en: Enables projects to efficiently develop their own financial processes.
Provides decisions support to ensure the right projects are launched.
Allows senior managers to delegate their governance responsibilities.
Ensures current projects are unaffected by changes to policy or strategy.

x.en: a P3O model increase an organization's ability to deliver its strategy Provides decisions support to ensure the right projects are launched.

q.en: Which of the following describe how an Organization Portfolio Office helps deliver change? 1-Allows the right resources to be allocated to the right programme and projects 2- Focuses on identifying changes that align best to strategic objectives 3- Monitors progress of programmes and projects against key organizational objectives 4-Is primarilly concerned with implementing the change correctly?

x.en: Organization Portfolio Office helps deliver change 1-Allows the right resources to be allocated to the right programme and projects 2- Focuses on identifying changes that align best to strategic objectives 3- Monitors progress of programmes and projects against key organizational objectives

q.en: Which is NOT an objective of a programme?

en: Coordinate related projects and activities
Align outcomes to strategic objectives
Deliver outcomes and benefits
Deliver business products according to a Business Case

x.en: Definition: programme management The coordinated organization, direction and implementation of a dossier of projects and transformation activities (i.e. the programme) to achieve outcomes and realize benefits of strategic importance. The focus of programme management is the delivery of outcomes and benefits that contribute to achieving the organization’s strategy. The Best Management Practice publication Managing Successful Programmes (MSP®‎) should be referred to for detailed guidance on the management of programmes (Cabinet Office, 2011).

q.en: Which receives the benefit of the governance provided by a P3O?

en: Change initiatives
Business as usual
Commercial
Finance

x.en: The benefit of the governance provided by a P3O (Change initiatives )

q.en: Which of the Best Management Practice principles for extracting value helps answer the question 'Are we getting the business benefits?'?

en: Prioritize investment
Govern effectively
Hold people to account
Safeguard value

x.en: Keyword (Benefit) so Benefit = Value Safeguard value ensures that business owners can identify via the benefits tracking service provided by a P3O whether the benefits are being achieved. Ref Tab 2.1

q.en: Which function or service should be provided by a COE?

en: Prioritizing the portfolio
Delivering programme communications
Managing knowledge
Monitoring programme risks

x.en: A COE typically provides knowledge management.

q.en: Which should be a responsibility of the P3O Sponsor role?

en: Providing effective financial control to the overall portfolio
Checking that products delivered by the portfolio are fit for purpose
Ensuring the P3O meets the needs of the main board
Providing a consistent approach to benefits and value management

x.en: Ensuring the P3O meets the needs of the main board This is one of the responsibilities of the P3O Sponsor and should be carried out by an individual. Ref App A.1.1

q.en: Which is MOST likely to be used as an individual tool?

en: Knowledge management systems
Spreadsheet software
Enterprise PPM software
Strategic mapping software

x.en: Desktop applications such as spreadsheets can be used in an individual manner with one user per business change initiative. Ref 5.2

q.en: Which of the following assist in identifying the current state of P3O services provided? 1. Analysing recent issues 2. Understanding the problems that need to be solved 3. Reviewing P3Os in other organizations 4. Analysing the results of reviews?

x.en: Reviewing P3Os in other organizations will not assist an organization in identifying their own current state of provision. Ref 2.4.2/2.4.2.1

q.en: Which action is recommended when implementing a P3O model?

en: Deliver the Blueprint in a single tranche of delivery
Treat the implementation as a change to processes rather than behaviour
Use programme management to run the implementation irrespective of the size or maturity of the organization
Use project or programme management processes to run the implementation

x.en: It is recommended that the implementation be run as a programme using Best Management Practice MSP or, at least, as a project. Ref 2.2/4.1.

q.en: Which is NOT created as part of the ‘Deliver’ process within the permanent P3O implementation lifecycle?

en: Transition
Post-implementation reviews
New capability
Stabilized operations

x.en: Post-implementation reviews Deliver is about delivering the new capability and realizing the benefits. Ref 4.3.3.1. Post-implementation reviews are part of Closure. Ref 4.2.4

q.en: Which P3O capability is MOST likely to reduce project delays?

en: Maximizing returns from investment
Ensuring there is no duplication of scope across programmes and projects
Coordinating change control processes across multiple projects
Identifying and managing interdependencies between programmes and projects

x.en: Identifying and managing interdependencies between programmes and projects ensures reduction in delays and prioritization of critical path activities.

q.en: Which are objectives of a COE?

en: Support the definition of a portfolio of change across an organization
Provide training and skills transfer to the PPM community in defined standards
Support the delivery of a portfolio of change in a geographical region
Support the delivery of a specific change initiative being delivered as a programme

x.en: A COE defines standards and provides skills and training.

q.en: What type of facilitated workshop is held for the purpose of identifying threats and opportunities?

en: Lesson sharing
Problem solving
Risk identification and risk assessment
Business solution

x.en: Risk identification and risk assessment This is the purpose of the risk identification and risk assessment workshop. Ref Tab 5.7

q.en: Where should an Organization Portfolio Office ultimately report?

en: Head of department
Corporate services function
Main board director
Divisional director

x.en: An Organization Portfolio Office should report to a main board director to add maximum value. Ref 3.2.1

q.en: Which of the following Key Performance Indicators provide evidence of the performance improvements delivered by a P3O? 1. Increased programme and project success rates 2. Improved portfolio balance 3. Increased organizational resource capacity 4. Enhanced contribution to the Benefits Realization Plan?

x.en: A P3O cannot add to resource capacity. Therefore, increased organizational resource capacity is not a P3O KPI. At best, the Resource Management role of the P3O will be able to summarize total resource capacity requirements and provide better intelligence about anticipated periods of resource shortfall and oversupply. Ref Tab 2.4/A.3.11.

q.en: Which skill or experience must the Head of an Organization Portfolio Office have?

en: Ability to manage portfolio finances
Extensive experience of knowledge management
Ability to write job descriptions for Portfolio Office staff
Credibility to work with middle and senior managers

x.en: The Head of P3O must be able to develop and maintain working relationships with senior managers and PPM teams. Ref A.1.2/Tab 3.5

q.en: Which of the following are created within the 'Identify ' process in the permanent P3O model lifecycle? 1. Outline of the future state vision of the P3O 2. Team structure for the on-going operation of the P3O 3. Initial justification of the investment in the P3O 4. Assessment of the current state of P3O services?

x.en: The team structure for the on-going operation of the P3O is defined in the ‘Define the P3O’ process as part of the Blueprint. Ref 4.2.2.4.2/Fig 4.1

q.en: What tool links projects to benefits, outcomes and strategy?

en: Strategic mapping software
Knowledge management systems
Requirements management systems
Enterprise architecture systems

x.en: Strategic mapping software maps projects to benefits, outcomes and strategy

q.en: P3O tools enable improved collaboration between programme team members working in different locations.’ Which key strategic benefit does this capability contribute towards?

en: Compliance to business process
Quality of decision support information
Decision-making
Management across geography

x.en: Improved management across geography is delivered through connectivity that allows for improvements to collaboration between project or programme team members. Ref 5.3

q.en: What functional role can also take on asset management?

en: Information Management
Finance
Change Control
Resource Management

x.en: The Information Management role may also take on asset management within the role as custodian and guardian of master copies of portfolio information.

q.en: Which statement describes the relationship between business as usual and change?

en: Decisions affecting either must consider both elements of an organization
They are separate activities that can survive independently
Change initiatives should always take priority
Business as usual should always take priority

x.en: Business as usual and change may be regarded as separate activities but cannot survive without each other. Therefore, any decisions relating to either need to be made collaboratively at the correct level. Ref 1.3.4

q.en: What tool links information in a hierarchical manner for multiple business change initiatives?

en: Individual
Assurance
Integrated
Collaborative

x.en: Integrated tools have the ability to link information in a hierarchical manner. The relationship is multiple business change initiatives to multiple users.

q.en: What element of the Blueprint should reflect the proposed reporting requirements for the future state P3O?

en: Risk Management Strategy
Risks to successfully setting up the P3O
Benefits Management Strategy
Organization structure

x.en: Reporting requirements must integrate with the organization structure in order to understand who needs what information. Ref 4.2.2.4

q.en: Which statement describes a P3O model with hub and spoke offices?

en: Portfolio, programme and project management standards unit, which defines standards, skills and training
Permanent, organization-level portfolio office supporting the delivery of change across an entire organization
Permanent, organization-level Portfolio Office linked to smaller permanent offices in different locations
Multiple locations with P3O functions carried out by a distributed team

x.en: Existing programmes and projects that are not aligned to strategy may be realigned or terminated or put on hold while higher priority initiatives which support strategy are delivered. Ref 1.3.1

q.en: What office within a P3O model needs staff members with investment management and strategic planning skills?

en: Project Office
COE
Programme Office
Organization Portfolio Office

x.en: The skills and competencies of the Portfolio Office staff will need to include investment management and strategic management. Ref 3.4.1/A.2.1.1

q.en: Which is a strategic planning function that a Portfolio Office should carry out?

en: Deploying project staff to manage the delivery of individual projects or programmes
Reviewing a risk which may affect multiple programmes and projects
Holding start-up workshops to fast-track projects or programmes
Developing a standard set of reporting templates for projects and programmes

x.en: Management of common risks at the portfolio level is a strategic planning / portfolio support function. Ref 3.3.2

q.en: What part of Business Change Governance answers the question 'Are we doing the right things?'?

en: Business Change Delivery
Business Change Strategy
Business Change Design
Business Change Value

x.en: Business Change Strategy answers the question ‘Are we doing the right things?’ Ref Fig 2.1

q.en: What is the sequence for the processes of the permanent P3O model implementation lifecycle?

en: Define; Identify; Deliver Capability / Realize Benefits; Close
Define; Identify; Close; Deliver Capability / Realize Benefits
Identify; Define; Deliver Capability / Realize Benefits; Close
Identify; Deliver Capability / Realize Benefits; Define; Close

x.en: The correct order is Identify; Define; Deliver Capability / Realize Benefits and then Close.

q.en: Which is a critical success factor when introducing standard tools to a P3O?

en: Ensure there is agreed accountability for the tool
Focus on the tool features rather than the value from using it
Ensure the sophistication of the tool drives the organizational capability
Identify how all the tool’s features can be used

x.en: The ownership of the tool must be agreed so that there is a single point of accountability for it. Ref 5.4

q.en: Which of the following statements about processes for an existing temporary office are true? 1. Defined information flows for the supported programme should be implemented 2. Resources within the Portfolio Office should be managed?

en: Neither 1 or 2 is true
Both 1 and 2 are true
Only 1 is true
Only 2 is true

x.en: The requirements of the programme as defined in the programme or project initiation document will drive the information flows and processes of the temporary Programme Office. Ref 4.3.2

q.en: What role implements procedures to collect data in a consistent format for programmes they support?

en: Quality Assurance
Programme Officer
Tools Expert
Programme Specialist

x.en: The Programme or Project Officer role implements guidelines, procedures and templates to collect and maintain consistent data and provides hands-on delivery support to a programme or project. Ref A.2.3.1/Tab 3.6

q.en: What types of office does a P3O typically consist of?

en: Permanent and temporary
Perpetual and temporary
Perpetual and transitory
Permanent and transitioning

x.en: A P3O can consist of permanent offices, temporary offices or a mixture of both.

q.en: Which stakeholder group is MOST likely to receive portfolio level reports?

en: Senior management / strategic planning
Business unit senior manager / Programme Board
External suppliers / stakeholders
Project Manager / delivery support

x.en: Senior management / strategic planning should receive portfolio level reports.

q.en: Which describes how a successful P3O model should operate?

en: With business as usual governance applied to all change initiatives within an organization
With awareness of other functions in the organization and how the P3O will work with them
Independently of all functions/departments in an organization
With line management responsibility for resources embedded from other functions

x.en: The Head of P3O needs to understand who is responsible for each of the functions performed within an organization and how the P3O will work with them. Ref 3.3.3

q.en: Which is a section in a Blueprint?

en: Risks to a P3O implementation
Business benefits
Information and data requirements
Standard templates

x.en: Information and data requirements This is a section of the Blueprint.

q.en: Which users of P3O services are MOST likely to need reassurance that change initiatives will be delivered with minimal disruption to operational plans?

en: Programme Manager
Third party suppliers
Head of P3O
The customer / user community

x.en: The customer/user community needs to be reassured that change will happen with least disruption to business as usual. Ref 2.4.2.2

q.en: What technique uses communities of practice to share learning?

en: Management dashboards
Project complexity modelling
Assurance, gated reviews and health checks
Knowledge management

x.en: Communities of practice are groups of people who work together to share their knowledge. Ref 5.6.4.2

q.en: Which of the following statements about a distributed model are true? 1. Staff are co-located 2. Team is distributed?

en: Only 2 is true
Neither 1 or 2 is true
Only 1 is true
Both 1 and 2 are true

x.en: Only 2 is true. Staff being physically co-located describes a physically co- located model. The team being distributed describes a distributed model. Ref 3.2.4

q.en: Which organizational factor has LEAST influence on the choice of P3O model?

en: Approach to organizational governance arrangements
Approach to service management
Number, size and duration of projects
Centralization versus decentralization of core services

x.en: Approach to service management is NOT a factor that influences the chosen model (Ref 3.1, ), although service management teams are a key stakeholder that the P3O should engage with during its operation. Ref 1.3.4

q.en: Which describes the treatment of information to comply with confidentiality, integrity and availability in Information Assurance?

en: Changed on the authority of the Head of the P3O
Checked by the P3O at project completion
Available to those who have authority to see it
Available to anyone who requests it

x.en: To ensure the correct availability of information, it should be accessible to those with the need and authority to access it. Ref 3.3.6

q.en: Which of the following are purposes of the Programme Specialist role? 1. Play a proactive role in sharing knowledge 2. Assist in implementing best programme management practice 3. Play a proactive role in promoting programme management methods 4. Improve programme monitoring by collecting and maintaining data in a consistent form?

x.en: Improving the planning and delivery process by collecting and maintaining data in a consistent form, is the purpose of the Programme or Project Officer role. Ref A.2.3/ Tab 3.6

q.en: Which of the following are attributes of gated reviews? 1. Are undertaken at key decision points in a programme or project 2. Assess how a programme is performing compared with its objectives 3. Establish the Key Performance Indicators for a programme or project 4. Check the quality of decision support information provided?

x.en: Key Performance Indicators are established for each change initiative when the programme, project or portfolio is first set up. They are not established by using the gated review technique. Ref 2.4.4.2

q.en: Which is NOT included within the definition of project management?

en: Motivating a team
Achieving outcomes
Monitoring a project
Planning a project

x.en: Programme management is the coordinated organization of a dossier of projects and transformation activities to achieve outcomes. Ref 1.3.2

q.en: How does a P3O model significantly contribute to an organization's chances of successfully delivering its strategy?

en: Makes decisions on the right priorities for the organization
Maintains an overview of all business change programmes and projects
Maintains the risk registers for the organization's projects
Provides advice and guidance on the day to day running of the business

x.en: Maintaining the big picture of the portfolio of programmes and projects (and the achievability and relative attractiveness of those initiatives) is one of the ways a P3O model contributes to successful delivery of strategy. Ref 2.2/5.6.1

q.en: What is the objective of the business process swimlanes technique?

en: Ensure the right skills are available to deliver business processes
Document standard, repeatable business processes
Analyse the benefits of implementing a P3O against the related costs
Define the processes to be followed by one project

x.en: The objective of developing business process swimlanes is to document standard and repeatable business processes with appropriate linkages. It is a specific P3O technique. Ref 5.6.8

q.en: Which activity occurs within the 'Define' process in the permanent P3O lifecycle?

en: Review progress at the end of each tranche
Document how the benefits of the P3O model will be tracked
Receive the original idea to enhance the P3O model
Appoint the Senior Responsible Owner to implement the enhanced P3O model

x.en: It is one of the activities of the ‘Define’ process to develop, model and validate the benefits recorded in Benefit Profiles. Ref 4.2.2.5

q.en: Which is an underlying success factor for a Virtual P3O model?

en: PPM standards owned by a senior PPM professional
A minimum P3M3 maturity level of 1 is achieved
Predictability of project and programme delivery is increased
Local variations to standards start to emerge

x.en: An underlying success factor for a Virtual P3O model is a single point of ownership by a senior PPM professional (head of profession for PPM) for portfolio, programme and project standards. Ref Tab 3.3

q.en: Which is provided by a P3M3 assessment when getting the investment for a P3O?

en: Understanding of the underlying PPM issues
Documented future state Blueprint
Replacement for a P3O Value Matrix
Identified and analysed stakeholders

x.en: P3M3 assessments provide a meaningful way to understand the underlying PPM issues and document the current PPM state. Ref 2.4.2.3

q.en: Which is NOT a likely threat to achieving a future state Blueprint?

en: Insufficient support from senior managers to recruit required skills
Resistance from PPM staff members who are impacted by the P3O implementation
More effective use of PPM resources
Use of inconsistent language by PPM staff members when implementing a P3O

x.en: More effective use of resources is a benefit driver that a P3O may provide. Ref 4.2.2.5

q.en: Which is a functional area within a P3O model?

en: Flexible resource pool
Model with hub and spoke offices
Virtual P3O model
COE services

x.en: The COE functions or services area is a functional area within a P3O model.

q.en: What does PPM stand for?

en: Project, Programme and Portfolio Matrix
Portfolio, Programme, Project Maturity
Portfolio, Programme and Project Management (including Value and Risk Management)
People, Process and Product Management (including Value and Risk Management)

x.en: The correct option follows directly from the guide's description of this element. Ref P3O guide.

q.en: Why should the outline Vision Statement provide a clear link to an organization’s business strategy?

en: Determine the governance to be applied to the P3O implementation programme
Document the processes that will be used to operate a P3O
Justify the investment in a P3O model
Connect the implementation of a P3O to an organization’s success

x.en: A clear link to the business strategy will show how these changes will contribute to an organization’s objectives. Ref 2.4.3

q.en: Which is a typical service offered as part of a delivery support function?

en: Supporting decision-making through management dashboards
Providing independent assurance of project delivery
Developing consistent working practices for PPM staff
Deploying experienced Project Managers to manage project delivery

x.en: The delivery support function may include a pool of professional Project Managers deployed temporarily to specific projects to manage their delivery. Ref 3.1

q.en: Which of the following statements about how the P3O size is influenced by organizational factors are true? 1. The size of the organization has little or no influence 2. The strategic objectives of the organization have an influence?

en: Only 2 is true
Neither 1 or 2 is true
Both 1 and 2 are true
Only 1 is true

x.en: The P3O size will depend on the business drivers it is set up to serve.

q.en: What does a P3O Business Case identify?

en: Value that a P3O model adds to the business change portfolio
Current PPM maturity
Detailed services that should be offered by the P3O model
Key stakeholders in the P3O implementation

x.en: The Business Case should answer the question ‘What value does it add to our investment portfolio?’ Ref 2.4.4.1

q.en: What service does a Temporary Office model provide to a programme?

en: Providing a flexible resource pool of programme staff
Setting standards for programmes to follow
Assisting Programme Managers in collecting data
Supporting prioritization of programmes within the portfolio

x.en: A Programme Officer should collect data in a consistent form as part of a Programme Office. Ref A.2.3.2. When a new programme is launched, it may require its own a temporary Programme Office. Ref 3.2.3

q.en: Which does NOT describe services delivered by the appropriate office within a P3O?

en: Portfolio Offices should facilitate the optimization of business change activities
Portfolio Offices should be compatible with business as usual governance structures
Programme Offices should assist in delivering programmes consistently and well
Project Offices should compare the consistency of different projects

x.en: Portfolio Offices and COEs, not Project Offices, support consistent delivery of change across an organization. A COE may also provide independent assurance to ensure this consistency. Ref Tab 1.2

q.en: Which non-PPM function may a P3O provide?

en: Provision of scrutiny and challenge of programme reports
Support in prioritizing investment
Secretariat service to management boards
Effective governance

x.en: A P3O may provide a secretariat service to management boards as a non-PPM function.

q.en: What should balance the value a P3O will give to an organization against the constraints?

en: Business Case
Blueprint
Stakeholder analysis
Phased implementation plan

x.en: When evaluating the benefits in the Business Case consideration should be given to the constraints which may constrain the P3O capability being achieved. Ref 2.4.4.1

q.en: Which is NOT a reason why a P3O should measure Key Performance Indicators?

en: Maintain commitment from stakeholders over time
Justify the programmes within the portfolio
Set overall targets for improvement
Measure success of a P3O implementation

x.en: It is a Business Case that is used to justify any investment decision. Ref 2.4.4.1

q.en: What should a P3O define in order to align its governance with the wider organization?

en: Corporate governance
Rules for escalating information
Information assurance
Non-PPM functions

x.en: Rules and routes for escalation and cascading of information need to be agreed and defined in order establish relationships with existing decision-making bodies. Ref 3.3.5

q.en: Why should recycling be done as part of implementing a temporary Project Office?

en: Recycle staff back into operations
Define the future state Blueprint for a Project Office
Justify the development of a permanent P3O
Identify methods that can be used by other Project Offices

x.en: Recycling is important to provide lessons and reusable elements for subsequent temporary offices to draw from. Ref 4.3.6

q.en: Which P3O model includes permanent decentralized offices with temporary Programme Offices, as required?

en: Delivery support
Model with Virtual P3O
Model with Hub and Spoke Offices
Model with Organization Portfolio Office

x.en: A P3O model with Hub and Spoke Offices has a permanent Portfolio Office with permanent decentralized offices which act as a Hub Portfolio Office to temporary programmes. Ref 3.2.2.2

q.en: How should internal resources be treated when appointed to a Project Office?

en: Have a career path developed as part of working in a P3O
Will work permanently in the Project Office
Acquire no additional skills before they return to operations
Have a temporary rise in status which should be removed when they return to operations

x.en: More careful consideration needs to be given to career development for individuals seconded to a project rather than buying in experienced people. Ref 4.3.4

q.en: What technique ensures that a programme is objectively assessed so that the lifecycle and governance applied are fit for purpose?

en: Knowledge management
Facilitation - workshop techniques
Complexity modelling
Gated reviews

x.en: The purpose of complexity modelling is to determine the appropriate lifecycle and governance for the programme based on its complexity. Ref 5.6.2

q.en: Why should rules relating to escalation of risks be agreed in a P3O model with multiple offices?

en: Allow every decision to be made at organizational board level
Enable multiple sources for a single piece of risk data
Enable a decision to be made by the right group based on the right information
Allow every Programme Manager to display risk information in a different way

x.en: Where a P3O comprises multiple offices, rules regarding escalation of risks should be established to ensure the right decision is taken by the right person or group based on the right supporting information. Ref 1.6

q.en: Which is a strategic planning function or portfolio support function?

en: Provision of a resource pool of delivery staff to programmes or projects
Development of standard methods and processes
Deployment of staff at programme or project start-up
Provision of support for escalated risks to support decision-making

x.en: Provision of support for decision-making may include escalated risks, issues changes, or information. This is a portfolio support / strategic planning function. Ref 3.1

q.en: Which is a common barrier that needs to be overcome to implement a P3O model successfully?

en: Standards aligned with external best practice
P3O senior management champion
Established programme management forum
Lack of focus on delivery of a full P3O model

x.en: Lack of focus on the full P3O model and only on a single P3O component is a common barrier that needs to be overcome. Ref 2.5

q.en: Which office triggers post-programme reviews to assess benefits?

en: Virtual
COE
Portfolio
Programme

x.en: The Portfolio Office triggers post-programme reviews to assess return on investment/benefits. Ref 1.5.1/Fig 1.3

q.en: Which describes an organization that typically adopts a Virtual P3O model successfully?

en: Has low levels of PPM maturity
Physical office supports decision-making
Has high levels of PPM maturity
Decision-making is centralized

x.en: The Virtual P3O model generally exists in organizations with high levels of PPM maturity where consistent standards are embedded. Ref 3.2.2.3

q.en: Which statement applies to stakeholders in the set-up of a temporary Programme Office and their needs?

en: Are the same as the stakeholders for the setting-up of a permanent P3O
Specifically include those involved in delivering the programme
Their needs are not analysed
Are only from other offices within the P3O

x.en: Stakeholders of a temporary Programme Office include Programme Board and programme team members. Ref 4.3

q.en: What technique provides an exception-based top-tier report with links to programme information?

en: Communities of practice
Complexity modelling
Management dashboards
Business process swimlanes

x.en: A management dashboard is generally provided as a top-tier report (exception- based) with links to programme information. Ref 5.6.3

q.en: What office is part of a centralized P3O model that can be used in any size of organization?

en: Organization Portfolio
Temporary
Virtual
Hub

x.en: An Organization Portfolio Office model is a centralized model that can occur in any size of organization. Ref 3.2.2.1

q.en: Providing an exception-based top-tier report with links to programme information is an important P3O Process, which P3O techniques is used for that?

en: Communities of practice
Business process swimlanes
Management dashboards
Complexity modelling

x.en: Ref 5.6.3, A management dashboard is generally provided as a top-tier report (exception- based) with links to programme information.

q.en: From the following functions or services, Which one should be provided by a COE?

en: Prioritizing the portfolio
Delivering programme communications
Managing knowledge
Monitoring programme risks

x.en: Ref 3.1, A COE typically provides knowledge management.

q.en: Which is an activity in the definition and implementation of a temporary Programme Office?

en: Design the future state Blueprint
Identify existing processes defined by the COE that may used
Transfer the realization of benefits to the operational environment
Create a Vision Statement for the office

x.en: Ref 4.3.2, COE may supply processes, templates and tools, and may assist in the setting up of information portals, collaboration and web-based tools etc. Where processes and templates are provided through a COE, consider whether they should be tailored to meet the needs of the particular programme or project being supported.

q.en: Which of the following is NOT a type of collaborative or integrated tool?

en: Performance management system
Strategic mapping software
Risk management system
Complex spreadsheet modeling

x.en: Ref 5.2, Desktop applications such as project planning software, word processing software or spreadsheets are examples of individual tools.

q.en: A lot of outcomes can be derived from different P3O capabilities. Which P3O capability offers the outcome of 'reduction of management overheard dealing with prioritization conflicts for resources'?

en: Enable the allocation of the right resources to the right programmes and projects
Proactive resolution of conflicts and competition for scarce and costly resources
Selection of the right programmes and projects
Enable maximization of returns from investment

x.en: Ref Table 2.2, 'Proactive resolution of conflicts and competition for scarce and costly resources 'capability will reflects on ' Reduction of management overhead dealing with prioritization conflicts for resources & Ability to plan the programmes and projects to make the best use of scarce resources, ensuring money is not wasted on expensive ‘just in time’ external resources'

q.en: Which high level function is most likely to provide the service of 'Commercial (including supplier) management'?

en: Centre of Excellence (COE)
Delivery (Programme and Project)
Planning (Portfolio)
This is more likely to come from the Procurement Team

x.en: Ref figure 3.4, It is all about getting the right service at the point where it is required - It is the Delivery function which is most likely to provide the service of Commercial (including supplier management) not Planning function.

q.en: Why do senior managers need to agree on which PPM problems they rate as critical?

en: Justifies to senior management the investment in a P3O
Defines a portfolio prioritization and optimization technique
Allows the P3O Sponsor to gain consensus on a common P3O vision
Justifies to senior management the investment in a P3O

x.en: Ref 2.4.2, Senior managers need to be asked which issues and problems they rate as critical. Consensus is required, preferably at the main board level. This ensures that the P3O sponsor understands what success looks like across the organization from differing viewpoints and allows them to gain consensus on a common P3O vision.

q.en: From the following P3O tools, which tools are used to align expected performance with strategic aims?

en: Strategic mapping software
Enterprise architecture systems
Performance management systems
Requirements management systems

x.en: Performance management systems align expected performance with strategic aims and track actual performance. Ref 5.5

q.en: Which should be documented in a Blueprint?

en: Actual Highlight Reports issued by individual projects
Need for Business Cases for mission-critical programmes to be reported to the Portfolio Board
Transition plans for the implementation of business change into business as usual
Benefit Profiles for individual benefits to be delivered by the P3O

x.en: Table 4.1, Mission-critical business cases to be reported to the Portfolio Board as An example of a P3O information flow which is included in Blueprint section 4 – Information and data requirements.

q.en: From the following P3O capabilities, Which capability is MOST likely to reduce risk, quicker starts, quicker to market, increase confidence in investment?

en: Maximizing returns from investment
Selection of the right programmes and projects
Identifying and managing interdependencies between programmes and projects
Ensuring there is no duplication of scope across programmes and projects

x.en: Ref Tab 2.2, Enabling " Selection of the right programmes and projects " P3O capability drive to Reduced risk, quicker starts, quicker to market, increased confidence in investment

q.en: Which is a responsibility of the P3O Sponsor role?

en: Ensure the portfolio delivers the required strategy
Recruit the Portfolio Office staff members
Secure the investment required to set up the P3O
Recommend an appropriate mix of programmes and projects

x.en: Table 3.5, The P3O sponsor is a senior manager who directs and champions the establishment and evolving operation of the P3O. They will ideally be a member of the main board. The P3O sponsor is accountable for developing and maintaining a viable business case to secure the investment required to implement and run the P3O model. The P3O sponsor may also fulfil the role of portfolio director.

q.en: For the purpose of determining the key benefits for a programme in the definition stage, What type of the following facilitated workshops is held?

en: MoV study
Stakeholder identification and communications planning
Dependency workshops
Benefits identification and modelling

x.en: Ref Tab 5.7, Benefits identification and modelling workshops are Held to determining the key benefits for a programme in the definition stage. Involves identifying the planned benefits and then determining the dependency network for the identified benefits. Can also collect input for benefit profile information

q.en: From the following P3O roles, Which one develop and maintain management dashboards.?

en: The tools expert role
The Programme or project specialist
Head of P3O
The Portfolio analyst

x.en: Ref Table 3.6, The Portfolio analyst develop and maintain management dashboards.

q.en: Which is an area where improvement targets and related Key Performance Indicators should be set?

en: Greater independence from strategic objectives
Improved portfolio balance in terms of overall risk and lifecycle stages
Increased number of programmes scoring amber or red at a gated review
Increased number of programmes scoring amber or red at a gated review

x.en: Ref 2.4.4.2, As a minimum, improvement targets and associated KPIs should be set for areas include ' Improved portfolio balance – in terms of overall risk, programme and project lifecycle stages, strategic alignment and investment type'

q.en: From the following responsibilities, Which one should be a responsibility of the head of programme or project office?

en: Checking that products delivered by the portfolio are fit for purpose
Establishes and runs the programme or project office.
Providing a consistent approach to benefits and value management
Providing effective financial control to the overall portfolio

x.en: Ref Table 3.5, The head of programme or project office establishes and runs the office.

q.en: Benefits map showing the relationships between outputs, capabilities, outcomes and benefits. Which element of P3O should be included in a benefits map?

en: The pace of change
Budget restrictions
Portfolio benefits management framework
Line management responsibility for resources embedded from other functions

x.en: Ref 2.4.4.1 and Table 2.3, Benefits map shows the relationship between outputs and benefits.

q.en: Where may standard techniques for a P3O exist in an organization?

en: Within a Business Case
As part of the P3O implementation plan
Reported in management dashboards
Within corporate standards and policies

x.en: Ref 5.2, Standard techniques for the P3O can be found in a number of places within the organization, such as: ' Within corporate or P3O standards and policies'

q.en: Which is a key activity of the Identify' process in the permanent P3O lifecycle?

en: Analysing stakeholders and planning communications
Delivering the new capability
Assessing the current state of P3O provision
Planning tranches of delivery

x.en: Ref 4.2.1, The key activity of the Identify' process in the permanent P3O lifecycle is 'Current state assessment'

q.en: Are we getting things done well?', What part of Business Change Governance answers this question?

en: Business Change Value
Business Change Design
Business Change Delivery
Business Change Strategy

x.en: Ref Fig 2.1, Business Change Delivery answers the question 'Are we getting things done well?'

q.en: Which is NOT a typical Key Performance Indicator which can be used to measure the success of a P3O?

en: Improved portfolio balance in relation to spend on short term contract resource
Increased success of programmes delivering to budget
Increased use of implemented tools by operations staff
Enhanced contribution measured against the Benefits Realization Plan

x.en: Ref 2.4.4.2, As a minimum, improvement targets and associated KPIs should be set for the following areas: 1- Overall programme and project success rates in relation to capital cost, duration, operating cost and benefits realization for each portfolio 2- Improved portfolio balance – in terms of overall risk, programme and project lifecycle stages, strategic alignment and investment type 3- Enhanced contribution to strategic objectives.

q.en: From the following P3O roles, Which one is providing a consultancy service to programme and project managers or programme and project boards?

en: The tools expert role
Portfolio analyst
The Programme or project specialist
Head of P3O

x.en: Ref Table 3.6, The Programme or project specialist (internal consultant) provide a consultancy service to programme and project managers or programme and project boards, delivering hands-on assistance to support the successful delivery of the programme or project.

q.en: Which of the following tools is MOST likely to be used as an Integrated tool?

en: Word processing software
Web-based portals
Enterprise PPM software
Project planning software

x.en: Ref 5.2, The relationship in Integrated tools is multiple business change initiatives to multiple users. Enterprise PPM software, which is distributed across an entire organization, is an example.

q.en: What are the following statements refer to? 1. Maintaining a 'big picture' understanding of the business change portfolio 2. Providing decision-support to ensure the right programmes and project are launched 3. Providing standards and processes to ensure consistency of delivery 4. Providing independent oversight, scrutiny and challenge to ensure things are done well (and right first time more of the time)?

en: Proposed responsibilities for the Temporary Portfolio Office
Time must be made senior managers to understand each of these things
OGC principles for extracting value from programme and project investment
Ways the P3O can significantly increase an organizations chances of successfully delivering its strategy reducing benefits loss and delivering programmes and projects more cost effectively

x.en: Ref 2.1, ' P3O can significantly increase an organizations chances of successfully delivering its strategy, reducing benefits loss and delivering programmes and projects more cost effectively ' by those ways.

q.en: Which P3O role implements procedures to collect data in a consistent format for programmes they support?

en: Programme Specialist
Programme Officer
Tools Expert
Quality Assurance

x.en: Ref A.2.3.1/Tab 3.6, The Programme or Project Officer role implements guidelines, procedures and templates to collect and maintain consistent data and provides hands-on delivery support to a programme or project.

q.en: Which is a typical constraint which impacts on how a P3O is implemented?

en: P3O assurance services must be independent
Pace of change must take into account current P3M3 maturity
P3O governance must align with existing corporate governance
Quality, standardized programme data is needed

x.en: Ref 2.4.4, Examples of these constraints are: Pace of change, The implementation of the P3O model must be matched to the organization’s ability to adapt to change and will need to take into account any other change initiatives under way. There is little point in creating a vision statement that seeks to achieve P3M3 Level 5 maturity for portfolio management across the organization within 18 months if the organization is currently at P3M3 Level 1 maturity.

q.en: Why should staff delivering non-PPM functions within a P3O model be treated as distinct administrative resources?

en: Provide non-PPM functions with a logical home
Meet business efficiency needs
Avoid discouraging people from choosing a career within a P3O
Deliver a secretariat service to management boards

x.en: Ref 3.7, Where the P3O provides non-PPM functions and services, it is important to ring-fence these administration resources away from the professional PPM functions in a separate team. If the P3O is seen as nothing more than an administration office, it may discourage people from deciding on a potentially rewarding career within a P3O.

q.en: In the permanent P3O model implementation lifecycle, What is the sequence for the processes?

en: Define; Identify; Close; Deliver Capability / Realize Benefits
Identify; Define; Deliver Capability / Realize Benefits; Close
Identify; Deliver Capability / Realize Benefits; Define; Close
Define; Identify; Deliver Capability / Realize Benefits; Close

x.en: Ref Fig 4.1, The correct order is Identify; Define; Deliver Capability / Realize Benefits and then Close.

q.en: Which tool provides integrated reports for multiple users from a single source of data?

en: Facilitated workshops
Enterprise PPM solutions
Benefit realization
Complexity modelling

x.en: Ref 5.5.1, The enterprise PPM solutions provide a single systems solution for programme and project data collection, maintenance and reporting, allowing for roll-up of information from a single source of data (one version of the truth) to programme and portfolio levels.

q.en: In the P3O Value Matrix, Which is an example of an enabling /support activity?

en: Checking whether the delivery of initiatives is on schedule
Managing the delivery of programmes
Acting as ‘Information hub’
Ensuring programme outcomes are in line with business strategy

x.en: Ref 2.4.2.2/Fig 2.2, Acting as ‘Information hub’ for the amalgamation of the project portfolio and provision of decision support for senior management is a support/enabling activity.

q.en: Providing an independent assessment of how well the portfolio, programme or project is performing relative to its objectives and any relevant process or standards, which P3O techniques is used for that?

en: Capacity planning for resource management
Skills development and maintenance
Assurance, gated reviews and health checks
Facilitation – workshops

x.en: Ref 5.6.10, The aim of assurance, gated reviews and health checks is to provide an independent assessment of how well the portfolio, programme or project is performing relative to its objectives and any relevant process or standards.

q.en: What type of a P3O role is a Project Officer?

en: Management
Generic
Functional
Consultancy

x.en: Ref Tab 3.6, A Project Officer is a generic role.

q.en: Which of the following are KPIs provide evidence of the performance improvements delivered by a P3O? 1. Enhanced contribution to the Benefits Realization Plan 2. Improved portfolio balance 3. Increased organizational resource capacity 4. Increased programme and project success rates?

x.en: A P3O cannot add to resource capacity. Therefore, increased organizational resource capacity is not a P3O KPI. At best, the Resource Management role of the P3O will be able to summarize total resource capacity requirements and provide better intelligence about anticipated periods of resource shortfall and oversupply.

q.en: Ensuring that the appropriate competencies are available across the organization to match against portfolio, programme or project, or requirements., which P3O techniques is used for that?

en: Facilitation – workshops
Skills development and maintenance
Complexity modelling
Knowledge management

x.en: Ref 5.6.7, The objective of skills development and maintenance is to ensure that the appropriate competencies are available across the organization to match against portfolio, programme or project, or requirements.

q.en: The change initiatives will be delivered with minimal disruption to operational plans, Which users of P3O services are MOST likely to need reassurance that?

en: The customer / user community
Head of P3O
Third party suppliers
Programme Manager

x.en: Ref 2.4.2.2, The customer/user community needs to be reassured that change will happen with least disruption to business as usual. Ref 2.4.2.2

q.en: Regarding to how the P3O size is influenced by organizational factors, Which of the following statements are true? 1. The strategic objectives of the organization have an influence 2. The size of the organization has little or no influence?

en: Only 1 is true
Both 1 and 2 are true
Only 2 is true
Neither 1 or 2 is true

x.en: Ref 3.1/3.5, Option 1 is true. The P3O size will depend on the business drivers it is set up to serve.

q.en: Regarding to the Best Management Practice principles for extracting value, Which of the following principles to Develop training, coaching and mentoring approaches for all roles within the PPM environment?

en: Invest in people and process
Govern effectively
Track progress through highlight and exception-based reporting
Safeguard value

x.en: Ref Table 2.1, Invest in people and process principle, P3O develop tailored approaches based on Best Management Practice approaches and ensure they are easily accessible to everybody in the PPM community. Develop training, coaching and mentoring approaches for all roles within the PPM environment.etc.

q.en: Which is a delivery support function offered within a P3O?

en: Reporting on progress through management dashboards
Alignment of change initiatives to strategy
Provision of independent assurance of programmes
Provision of project support resources to projects

x.en: Ref 3.3.2, Within the delivery support functional area, programme planning is concerned with understanding the new capability that will be required to realize planned business benefits, how it will be delivered and when, whilst ensuring that delivery resources are available and economic. It also covers dependency management, both within the programme and to other external factors.

q.en: Which technique can include the use of ad hoc reviews?

en: Facilitated workshops
Management Dashboards
Assurance, Gated Reviews and health checks
Knowledge Management

x.en: Ref 5.6.4.2, The most common knowledge management techniques are Communities of practice, Lessons, Archiving of portfolio, programme and project good practice, and learning reviews. The two most common types of review are ad hoc (often called after-action reviews) and planned reviews (e.g. the post-implementation review).

q.en: As a part of a delivery support function, Which is a typical service offered?

en: Deploying experienced Project Managers to manage project delivery
Supporting decision-making through management dashboards
Providing independent assurance of project delivery
Developing consistent working practices for PPM staff

x.en: Ref 3.1, The delivery support function may include a pool of professional Project Managers deployed temporarily to specific projects to manage their delivery.

q.en: Which P3O capability is MOST likely to lead to unviable projects being stopped at the initial investment gate?

en: Selection of the right programmes and projects via an established structure
Identification of potential duplication of scope or double counting of benefits
Coordinated change control process across multiple projects and business operations
Tracking of progress on programmes against key outcomes

x.en: Table 2.2, one of the outcomes of 'Selection of the right programmes and projects' P3O capability is Pet or rogue projects stopped at the initial investment stage gate.

q.en: From the following P3O roles, Which one provides support to the PPM community to configure software or provide training and coaching in its use?

en: The Finance role
Tools expert role
The Programme or project specialist
Head of P3O

x.en: Ref Table 3.7, The Tools expert role is an expert in software tools to support the change environment. The role may provide support to the PPM community to configure software or provide training and coaching in its use.

q.en: During the permanent P3O implementation lifecycle, Which is NOT created as part of the ‘Identify’ process?

en: Objectives and goals
Outline vision statement
Outline business case
Develop the P3O blueprint

x.en: Ref 4.2.1, The key activities within the Identify process are as follows: Current state assessment, Outline vision statement, Objectives and goals, Outline business case(including risks)

q.en: Which is NOT a use of integrated tools?

en: Links information across business change initiatives in a hierarchical manner
Allows multiple people to access multiple sets of information
Supports a single business change initiative with multiple users
Uses a single installation of the tool across the organization

x.en: Ref 5.2, Integrated Tools: Where multiple people access multiple sets of information that are integrated in some manner through a tool. There will generally be a single installation or instance of the tool across the organization, with partitions for business change initiatives and the ability to link information in a hierarchical manner. The relationship is multiple business change initiatives to multiple users.

q.en: During the set-up of a temporary Programme Office and their needs, which statement applies to stakeholders?

en: Specifically include those involved in delivering the programme
Are only from other offices within the P3O
Their needs are not analysed
Are the same as the stakeholders for the setting-up of a permanent P3O

x.en: Ref 4.3, Stakeholders of a temporary Programme Office include Programme Board and programme team members.

q.en: Which is a purpose of the Head of P3O role?

en: Ensure the organization carries out the role of Informed Customer
Provide a consultancy service to Programme and Project Managers
Ensure alignment with wider policy and strategic initiatives
Facilitate the development of an optimized portfolio

x.en: Table 3.5, The Head of P3O role provide strategic challenge, overview and scrutiny, ensuring alignment with wider policy and strategic initiatives.

q.en: Understanding the resource capacity and competency supply-and demand levels and take action to match these appropriately to meet delivery requirements., which P3O techniques is used for that?

en: Facilitation – workshops
Capacity planning for resource management
Skills development and maintenance
Business process swimlanes

x.en: Ref 5.6.9, The objective of capacity planning for resource management at the portfolio level is to understand the resource capacity and competency supply-and demand levels and take action to match these appropriately to meet delivery requirements.

q.en: From the following responsibilities, Which one should be a responsibility of commercial role?

en: Ensure the organization carries out the role of informed customer.
Checking that products delivered by the portfolio are fit for purpose
Ensures stakeholder analysis is undertaken regularly
An expert in software tools to support the change environment

x.en: Ref Table 3.7, The commercial role is to ensure the organization carries out the role of informed customer and all commercial/procurement practices and decisions meet designated standards and offer the organization ‘value for money’.

q.en: What is used to assist senior managers to determine their core problems and the services to be delivered by a P3O model?

en: Capacity planning for resource management
Business process swimlanes
Knowledge management tools
P3O Value Matrix

x.en: Ref 2.4.2.2, The P3O value matrix: A simple technique to assist senior managers in determining their core problems and agreeing the value and scope of the P3O model is the P3O value matrix.The matrix considers portfolios, programmes and projects – and provides a high-level description of the potential role a P3O can play in providing governance over both enabling and restraining activities, across the three levels.

q.en: Which of the following is true for Programme or Project Specialist (Internal Consultant) role?

en: It is a generic role
It must never be carried out on a Part-time basis
It must only be carried out on a Part-time basis
It is a functional role

x.en: Ref Table 3.6, The Programme or Project Specialist (Internal Consultant) role is a Management and generic role.

q.en: Document standard and repeatable business processes with appropriate linkages and agreed accountabilities., which P3O techniques is used for that?

en: Business process swimlanes
P3O information portal
Skills development and maintenance
Facilitation – workshops

x.en: Ref 5.6.8, The objective of developing business-process swimlanes is to document standard and repeatable business processes with appropriate linkages (often across multiple divisions or business units within an organization) and agreed accountabilities.

q.en: Which section in the Blueprint should reflect the proposed reporting requirements for the future state P3O?

en: Benefits Management Strategy
Organization structure
Risk Management Strategy
Risks to successfully setting up the P3O

x.en: Ref 4.2.2.4, Reporting requirements must integrate with the organization structure in order to understand who needs what information.

q.en: Which key strategic benefit does the next capability contribute towards? ‘P3O tools enable improved collaboration between programme team members working in different locations.’?

en: Management across geography

x.en: 3.3.6 Information assurance The value of information assurance (IA) varies from organization to organization. Organizations such as the Ministry of Defence, the banking industry and others working with personal or sensitive information understand that it is critical to their business, and they invest significant time and money to maintain robust processes, procedures and systems in this area. The Data Protection Act and the Freedom of Information legislation define minimum statutory guidelines for all organizations. This has implications for all portfolio, programme and project information. IA is based on the three concepts of confidentiality, integrity and availability. These terms mean that: information is only available to those who have a need and the authority to see it; only those with the correct authority are able to change information; and the information is available whenever and wherever the business requires it to be. The P3O has a crucial cost-effective role in providing a number of IA-related resources and management functions for the support of all areas of the PPM environment. Consideration of the IA requirements for the project and its outputs must start at the beginning of the project. Trying to build in IA measures or take remedial action to deal with identified IA issues at the end of the project will never be as cost-effective or as efficient as building them in during development. The P3O can ensure that an appropriate initial assessment of the IA issues is carried out during the initiation stage of any new activity. Page 55, Design P3O Model

A frequent reason for the failure of permanent P3Os is a lack of integration of the P3O model with the wider organization model. The head of P3O needs to understand who is responsible for the various functions and how the model, and the various offices within it, will interact with them. These other functions include: ■ Strategy development and management, including business planning ■ IT service management (release, change, configuration etc.) ■ Human resources ■ Marketing/public relations ■ Procurement/purchasing/commercial, including bid management ■ Finance ■ Corporate risk management ■ Corporate information assurance (see section 3.3.6 for further information) ■ Audit ■ Quality ■ Business operations. Just as P3O resources may exist in a matrix management environment with local business line management but a professional link to an organization portfolio office or COE, so will other professional resources. Clarity is required in terms of roles/responsibilities for delivering functions and services across business areas. For example, financial functions and services may be provided through a temporary programme office, but the person delivering the service may be embedded in the programme office, with their line management and the standards for financial reporting developed and specified by the finance department. Embedded resources are temporarily assigned to a programme or project (either full-time or part-time), but their originating department still controls the processes that they will follow and is responsible for normal line management activities. increased ability to bundle related requests for change for programmes

Reduction in overheads dealing with conflicting resources

q.en: Which is NOT a specific area where KPIs should be set as a minimum to measure a P3O model's success?

en: Reduced cost of skilled resources
Improved portfolio balance in terms of overall risk
Enhanced contribution to strategic objectives
Increased overall programme success rates in relation to benefits realization

x.en: As a minimum, improvement targets and associated KPIs should be set for the following areas: ■ Overall programme and project success rates in relation to capital cost, duration, operating cost and benefits realization for each portfolio ■ Improved portfolio balance – in terms of overall risk, programme and project lifecycle stages, strategic alignment and investment type ■ Enhanced contribution to strategic objectives. Improving the portfolio balance will involve not only developing the right mix of programmes and projects but also avoiding the scenario where multiple programmes and projects: ■ Are in the start-up process at the same time ■ Are intended to deliver key outputs into a business function simultaneously ■ Require limited resources at the same time. KPIs should be SMART: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound. Page 33, Why have a P3O.

q.en: Who does a P3O support by providing practical hands-on help?

en: Suppliers
Senior managers
Customer / User community
Programme and Project managers

x.en: Programme or project specialist (internal consultant) The specialist provides hands-on support for programme and project managers and plays a proactive knowledge management role in the promotion of programme and project management methods, and the roll-out of Best Management Practice. They provide a consultancy service to programme and project managers or programme and project boards, delivering hands-on assistance to support the successful delivery of the programme or project. This consultancy may take the form of coaching, help, advice and guidance, or may be of a specific nature in the form of facilitated workshops.

q.en: Which does NOT describe how services are provided within a Virtual P3O model?

en: Resources are in a single P3O office within a central corporate function
Resources use embedded consistent standards
Professional staff are embedded within business teams
Staff work across an organization without a physical structure to support them

x.en: 3.2.2.3 Virtual P3O model The ultimate decentralized model is the virtual P3O model, where there is no permanent office. P3O functions and services are embedded in the organization’s business delivery units, with portfolio activities undertaken by a central strategy or business-planning office or within the finance department. Temporary programme and project offices are established to support initiatives as they are launched, and these offices are staffed and supported from within the business units themselves. This model generally exists in organizations with a high level of PPM maturity, where consistent standards are embedded, the PPM resources are highly competent, and P3O functions and services can be provided across the organization without the need for a physical structure to support them. There is often a head of profession for portfolio, programme and project management, who liaises with all the professional staff embedded within business teams. This role also provides the link to strategy and business planning, and ensures that internal standards remain aligned with good practice through attendance at best-practice events, seminars etc. A key feature of this model is its use of programme, risk and project management forums/ communities of practice, where all PPM professionals come together at regular events to share best practice and learn about new methods and ways of working.

q.en: Which is NOT a way that tools are typically used?

en: Connected
Collaborative
Integrated
Individual

x.en: Tools may be used in the following ways ■ Individual Where only one person (generally the project manager) uses the tool. There may be multiple installations or instances of the tool across the organization but the relationship is generally one business change initiative to one user. Desktop applications such as project planning software, word processing software or spreadsheets are examples. ■ Collaborative Where multiple people access a single set of information through a tool. A temporary flexible organization structure created to coordinate, direct and oversee the implementation of a set of related projects and activities
The totality of an organization's investment in the changes required to achieve its strategic objectives
The way the business normally achieves its objectives

Programme office
Project office

Business as usual governance does not apply to change initiatives
